lead: IonQ / IONQ — buy the quantum dip
smaller: Nebius / NBIS — retail's elated over the data centre
Silver / SLV — the squeeze is coming
Dogecoin / DOGE-USD — the meme coin dream is fading
why_lead: Rheinmetall was replaced. Its angle is the 5 March lead's: Europe's rearmament, the EU's 800bn euro plan and the German debt-brake deal, and the same 3 March Bankier 'hottest commodity' and Investing.com Polska pieces are re-cited (the same articles, under new IDs). The only new attention item, Reuters on 6 March, concerns Eutelsat, not Rheinmetall. IonQ is the best-supported distinct lead: IonQ closed at 20.48 dollars, down 9.50 percent in the prior session, 17.78 percent over five sessions and 51.61 percent over 20, while the company's own news on 4 and 5 March (ID Quantique acquisition, a US Air Force Research Lab system, faster gates) kept coming and IBD on 6 March ties the crash to Nvidia's chief executive. The 3 March smaller sold the million-dollar target with the ID Quantique deal still described as talks, so the story has changed.
why_smaller: Nebius / NBIS is new. Stocktwits on 5 March has retail elated at the 300MW New Jersey plan, and the stock then fell 11.17 percent in the prior session and is 21.01 percent below its 20-session reference: a reversal, not a repeat.

Silver / SLV is unchanged from the draft and is new to the window: dated squeeze talk from Kitco on 6 March, the Economist's silver-is-the-new-gold line on 5 March, and SLV up 4.54 percent over five sessions. It is the non-equity trade.

Dogecoin / DOGE-USD is a failed narrative with dated items on 4, 5 and 6 March (the STAR10 drop, the memecoin market down 56 percent, Trump's coin down 81 percent) and DOGE down 25.82 percent over 20 sessions. The 3 March edition noted a fizzling meme-coin mood only through a 1 March item, so today's numbers are new.
considered_not_chosen: Rheinmetall (5 March lead): same angle and same articles re-cited under new IDs; the new Reuters item concerns Eutelsat, a different company. Not a lead again, and not carried as a smaller because the slots went to new narratives.

XRP: the 3 March lead's reserve story, now the fourth reserve-themed item since 3 March (Solana 4 March, bitcoin 6 March). The reserve reveal is still pending, the Barron's piece is commentary, and the move is a price bounce alone.

Palantir: a real reversal (the 6 March DOGE-talk smaller, then a Karp share-sale headline dated 6 March and a 10.73 percent fall in the prior session), but a repeat one day later, and the crowd is leaving rather than buying the dip, so it fails the lead test.
Hims & Hers: a 6 March Barron's sell call and a -15.90 percent prior session, but the attention is analyst-only, with no retail item in the window.
Tesla: smaller on 3, 4, 5 and 6 March; no changed story justifies a fifth.
Alibaba: the 6 March lead; the Hong Kong +8.39 percent session is a second leg, not a new story for a lead on consecutive days.
Eutelsat: its 650 percent surge is in a 6 March Reuters headline only, and Eutelsat is not on the market data, so it cannot carry a price.
AST SpaceMobile: 5 March smaller; the new GameStop-effect item is about Eutelsat, so the Starlink-rival story has not changed enough to repeat.
Xeris, Ocugen, Adma, Emergent, Beam: Stocktwits and Yahoo items, but none is on the market data, so no price or horizon can be used.
